info.title: Orbitwrite API
info.description: The part of the Orbitwrite API this plugin calls. Generated by scripts/sync-openapi.mjs; do not edit by hand.

get.summary: Identify the workspace behind the API key
get.description: Returns the organization the API key is scoped to — or, for an OAuth access token (`orbitwrite login`), the workspace the person signed in to. Used by integrations (e.g. Zapier) to test the connection and label it.

Every channel in the workspace, live and disconnected, in a stable order. Read this rather than deriving channels from a page's own data when you need one channel by id — the caller then doesn't have to already hold the list. Tokens are never returned.

get.description: What each platform a channel can be connected to accepts: character limits (and the premium ceiling, for X Premium), whether threads are allowed, media limits (count, types, sizes, video length, frame rate, aspect ratio), the `postFormat` values it offers and what each narrows, polls, quotes, reply settings and the JSON Schema of its `platformOptions`. The server enforces every rule here; read it to shape a post before sending. Any credential is served, whatever its scopes.

maxChars.description: Per post, or per thread item.

premiumMaxChars.description: The ceiling for a premium account (X Premium), when the platform has one.

withMediaMaxChars.description: A tighter ceiling when the post carries media (Telegram captions).

commentMaxChars.description: The ceiling for an auto-comment, when tighter than a post.

threads.description: Whether a post may be a chain of items. Each item has the text limit; there is no cap on the number of items.

maxItems.description: Attachments per post (per thread item). 0: none.

required.description: A post without media is refused.

exclusive.description: A video takes the whole post: no other media beside it.

externalGifs.description: Accepts a GIF from GIF search.

gifExclusive.description: A GIF takes the whole post. any: every GIF; picked: a GIF from GIF search. Null: GIFs mix with other media.

document.description: A single document (PDF) in place of media. Null: no documents.

publishesText.description: False: the text is not published (an Instagram story has no caption).

formats.description: The `postFormat` values this platform offers, default first, with what each narrows. Empty: feed posts only.

replies.description: Accepts a `replyToUrl`: publishing as a reply to an existing post.

replySettings.description: Values for `replySettings` (who may reply). Empty: not settable.

schema.description: JSON Schema of the options object.

field.description: The boolean field under that key; set it to `true` to label the post.

aiLabel.description: Where to label a post as AI-generated, so the network shows its own AI label on it. Null: the network's API has no such label. Read the field's description in `options.schema`: YouTube's covers realistic altered or synthetic content only, and X's applies to posts with media.

get.description: Candidate times to schedule a post at, one entry per connected channel. The slot strategies return the workspace's configured posting slots that nothing is scheduled on yet — the same placement the composer's queue makes, so a caller and the calendar agree on which slots are free. `best-time` instead ranks a static, research-informed engagement profile for the platform; it is a heuristic, not measured analytics (`researched` says whether the platform has a profile of its own or the generic fallback). Requires `postingSchedule:read` and `account:read`; the slot strategies also require `post:read`, since occupancy is post data.

post.description:
The composer's schedule/publish submit, and the way an integration creates posts. Validates platform capabilities, quote/reply targets, media URL safety, and engagement accounts; splits accounts into composer groups (synced accounts share one, each unsynced account gets its own); optionally replaces an existing group (re-schedule) or attaches a reviewer approval to each new group. With `publishNow` the adapter publish runs detached after the rows commit.

Media can be attached inline via an item's `media` (`{url, mimeType, …}`), or by id via `mediaIds` for files uploaded through `/media/create-upload-url`. Ids are resolved server-side and appended to that item's `media`; both forms can be used together, and up to 10 ids are accepted per item.

Authenticates with a workspace API key or a session cookie. The accounts posted to must all belong to the key's workspace; the posts are attributed to the user who created the key.

isAigc.description: Label as AI-generated ("Creator labeled as AI-generated").

topicTag.description: The post's topic (Threads' `topic_tag`): 1 to 50 characters, no periods or ampersands. A leading # is ignored. Set on the first post of a thread only.

containsSyntheticMedia.description: Altered or synthetic content: realistic video made or changed with AI (a real person, place or event).

isAiGenerated.description: Label as AI-generated ("AI info"). Not applied to stories.

userTags.description: People tagged in the media, not caption @mentions. x/y: 0-1 from the photo's top left (default centre). mediaUrl: which attachment (default the first). 20 per item max, public accounts only.

collaborators.description: Up to 3 usernames invited as collaborators. Not applied to stories.

madeWithAi.description: Label "Made with AI". Sent only when the first post has media.

aiGenerated.description: Label as AI-generated where the network has a label (TikTok, Instagram, X, YouTube).

get.description: Every post in the workspace — drafts, awaiting approval, scheduled and published — one entry per composer group, so a post synced to eight channels is one row carrying eight accounts. Cursor-paged rather than offset-paged: a workspace gains posts at the head, so an offset would re-show rows while a client pages. Filters combine with AND; repeat a parameter for OR within it. For one post's full content — threads, per-channel bodies, media, engagement — read it back with `GET /posts/draft?groupId=`.

timezone.description: IANA zone the times were placed in — the workspace's, falling back to the channel's and then UTC.

times.description: Soonest first for the slot strategies, strongest first for best-time. Empty when the channel has no free slot inside the two-week lookahead.

reason.description: Why these times, for a best-time answer. Null for the slot strategies, where the reason is the workspace's own configuration.

researched.description: Whether `reason` reflects a profile researched for this platform or the generic fallback window. Best-time data is a heuristic either way — there is no per-account analytics behind it yet, so do not report it to a person as measured engagement.

AnalyticsMetricValues.description: Each metric summed; null where nothing reported it (Bluesky has no impressions, say), never 0 for 'unknown'.

historyDays.description: Set when the plan's analytics history cut the window short: how many days back it reaches.

previous.description: The window compared against: `compareFrom`/`compareTo` when given, else the same length of time just before the window. Null when the plan's history doesn't reach it.

value.description: Null when no post in the window reported it.

historyDays.description: Set when the plan's analytics history cut the window short: how many days back it reaches.

media.description: The post's first attachment, for a thumbnail, and how many it has. Null without media.

value.description: The ranked metric, summed over the post's channels.

AutomationDefaults.description: Stored defaults that seed the composer's auto-engagement panel for this channel; null when never configured.

handle.description: The channel's handle on its platform, as it was at connect time.

profileUrl.description: The channel's public profile page. Null where the platform has none (Discord, Slack) or the handle can't name one.

needsReconnect.description: The platform credentials are dead — the channel can't publish until it's reconnected.

inboxReconnectNeeded.description: LinkedIn Pages only: the grant predates the comment-read scope the inbox needs (`r_organization_social`). Publishing works; comments can't be pulled until the Page is reconnected.

defaultSelected.description: Pre-selected when a fresh post is composed.

disconnected.description: Disconnected from the workspace. Disconnecting is a soft revoke so the channel's posts survive, which is why these rows are returned rather than hidden: they still have to be reachable to reconnect or to clear their content.

isPremium.description: X Premium, which raises the composer's character limit from 280 to 25,000.

canShareToInstagram.description: Threads only: whether connect-time probing found the linked Instagram account eligible for cross-sharing. Null when unknown — an older connection, or a probe that failed — which the composer treats as "allow, and let the publish path decide".

primaryAccountId.description: The channel whose content the composer syncs to the others, or null when the workspace hasn't set one.

publishing.description: Present on publish-now: rows are committed and the adapter publish runs detached — poll /posts/publish-status with `groupIds`.

videoProcessing.description: True when an attached video is still processing. The post publishes automatically once it finishes; publish-now waits on it.

groupIds.description: Distinct composer groups created — one for the synced cluster plus one per unsynced account.

videoProcessing.description: True when an attached video is still processing. The post publishes automatically once it finishes; publish-now waits on it.

name.description: Original file name — kept for display and its extension.

size_bytes.description: Exact byte length of the file. Part of the signature — the PUT must send this many bytes with this Content-Type or storage rejects it.

organization_id.description: Required for session callers without an active organization. Ignored for API keys, which are already scoped to one workspace.

title.description: PDF documents only — LinkedIn requires a document title.

upload_url.description: Signed PUT URL. Send the raw bytes with the same Content-Type you declared. Expires — upload promptly.

size_bytes.description: Storage consumed by this asset, and what the usage meter sums. For a Stream video that is every rendition plus the HLS segments — several times the size of the single file `url` serves, which is `rendition_bytes`.

rendition_bytes.description: Byte length of the file at `url`. Video only, and null until the transcode has finished and it could be measured — an unmeasured video is not the same as an empty one. This is the number a platform's video budget applies to; `size_bytes` is not.

status.description: `pending` until the upload has been confirmed to have landed. Confirmation happens lazily when the record is read, so a freshly uploaded file reports `uploaded` from the first GET after the upload completes. `processing` applies to video only: the bytes have arrived but Bunny Stream is still transcoding, so no playable URL exists yet — treat it as not-yet-usable rather than as a failure.

url.description: Public CDN URL. Only serves bytes once the upload has completed.

nextCursor.description: Pass back as `cursor` for the next page; null on the last page. A cursor is tied to the `sort`/`direction` it was cut for — change either and start again without it.

platformUrl.description: This channel's permalink to the published post, once the network returned one.

status.description: This channel's own row, where a group's rows can differ (a partial publish leaves one channel published and another scheduled). The entry's `status` is the representative row's.

lastError.description: This channel's most recent worker error, suppressed once its row published. When the post repeats the channel across variants, the first variant's error that survives that suppression.

isEmpty.description: This channel's row has no text, media, poll or quote — a reserved slot or a blank draft, which the worker holds at fire time rather than publishing nothing. Per channel: a board flags the post when ANY channel's row is empty, not only the preview's. True when any of the channel's variants is empty.

charCount.description: Length of this channel's copy, in UTF-16 code units (what the composer counts). When the post repeats the channel across variants, `status`, `charCount` and `charLimit` come together from one variant: the first that is over its limit and can still fire (draft, scheduled or pending approval), otherwise the first.

charLimit.description: The platform's character limit for this channel, premium-aware (X Premium raises it) and media-aware (a row with attachments is held to the caption limit where the platform has one, as Telegram does). `charCount > charLimit` means the row won't publish as-is. Per channel because one synced body meets a different limit on each platform.

id.description: The composer group's id — what every group-addressed route (`/posts/draft`, `/posts/reschedule`, `/posts/discard`) takes.

postId.description: The representative row's own post id, for the post-addressed routes (`/posts/{postId}/analytics`).

text.description: The preview row's body — the representative row's, or `previewAccountId`'s when the post goes out on that channel. Per-channel bodies can differ; `GET /posts/draft?groupId=` returns them all, with threads and media.

approvalStatus.description: What the post READS as — its active approval request's status whether or not that request blocks. `bucket` is derived from this.

approvalGateStatus.description: The post's own approval column: the publish gate, which a non-blocking review never writes. Ask this when the question is 'would this publish?'.

bucket.description: Which board column the post sits in.

scheduledAt.description: ISO 8601 — the group's earliest fire time. Null for a draft that has never been given one.

boardPosition.description: Where a person placed the post in a hand-ordered board column (Drafts, Needs approval, Needs revision, Approved), higher first — set by `POST /posts/reorder`. Null until someone moves it; it then sorts by `createdAt` in epoch milliseconds, so the two share one key space. Scheduled and Posted are ordered by time instead.

previewAccountId.description: The channel whose row supplied `text`, `media` and `platformUrl`: the `previewAccountId` asked for when the post goes out on it, otherwise the representative row's channel.

media.description: The preview row's attachments, enough to draw thumbnails. When the post has no row on `previewAccountId` (or none was asked for) and the representative row has no attachments, the first channel's row that has some, so a card never shows no images for a post that has them.

quoteUrl.description: The post this one quotes, if any.

platformUrl.description: The preview row's permalink once published. Every channel's own is on `accounts`.

author.description: Who wrote the post; null if their account is gone.

lastError.description: Most recent worker error, suppressed once the post published (a retry that eventually succeeded leaves its error behind).

accountId.description: The channel it concerns, or null when it is the whole post's.

issues.description: Every reason the post won't publish as it stands, from the channels that can still go out (draft, scheduled, pending approval): `empty` (nothing to post, on the whole post or one channel), `reconnect` (the channel's credentials are dead), `over_limit`, `media_too_large`, `capability` (a format, attachment or option the network refuses), `auto_dm` (an enabled Auto-DM that isn't complete) and `invalid_poll`. The same list the app's composer shows for the post. Empty when there is nothing to fix; a worker's publish error is `lastError`, not one of these.

campaign.description: The campaign this post belongs to, if any.

accounts.description: Every channel this post goes out on.

score.description: The post's health-check score, 0–100 — the checklist `GET /posts/{groupId}/score` returns, kept per post and refreshed whenever the post changes. Null for a post with none of its channels still connected. Read `scoreGrade` for what it means; the number is a heuristic, not a measurement.

scoreGrade.description: The score's grade: excellent (90+), good (75+), fair (50+) or needs_work.

source.description: `slot` — a configured posting slot with nothing on it. `best-time` — a peak cell of the platform's engagement profile.
